statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk stays in the watch band, below the block threshold, while the environment remains high-stress and cross-asset confirmation has deteriorated.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH. The published danger window covers the quarter-end cash close from 19:00Z to 20:00Z, where power-hour flow and final-day-of-Q3 market-on-close imbalances overlap.
headline: Long-end yields reverse higher and semiconductors lag as the Nasdaq-100 fades off its high into the quarter-end close
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30556.73, up 217.39 points or 0.72%, roughly 61 points below the 30617.74 session high it set earlier; the 30415.16 session low was made near the 30421.68 open. The index has not extended in the past hour, so a retracement is in progress rather than a one-way path. The cross-asset backdrop has turned less supportive than it was at the previous assessment. The 10-year Treasury yield has given back its entire post-PCE decline and trades at 5.28, the top of its 5.20-5.28 daily range, while the 30-year reached 5.61%, its highest since 2002, and the Treasury market is on course for its worst September since 2023. WTI is $91.66, up 2.55% and close to its $91.76 session high, with the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption keeping energy bid. The PHLX Semiconductor Index has weakened to 12590.05, down 0.31% and near its 12555.65 session low, so the sector that normally confirms a Nasdaq-100 advance is not confirming it. Breadth is narrow: the Dow is close to unchanged while the Nasdaq Composite is up about 0.93%. Today's data were mixed for the long end. August core PCE cooled to a 0.2% monthly pace against about 0.3% expected and 3.0% year over year, but ADP private payrolls rose 90,000 in September against 70,000 expected, the Chicago PMI jumped to 58.8 against 51.2 expected, and final Q2 GDP growth was 2.2%, a combination that pushed yields back up despite the softer inflation print. Because the index path itself shows retracement and semiconductor and Dow breadth conflict with the advance, the observed evidence does not establish the persistent mean-reversion failure that Tail measures; the diverging cross-asset picture, multi-decade-high long-end yields and elevated energy raise Stress instead. This is the final session of Q3, so quarter-end rebalancing concentrates two-way imbalance risk into the 20:00Z cash close.

lookbackSummary: Published Claude assessments over the preceding 24 hours held Tail between 15 and 22. The mapping was green EA_ON from the late European session on September 29 through the Asian and European hours of September 30, with Stress easing from the low 70s to about 65 overnight. The state moved back into the watch band from 12:35Z as the US pre-open and the August PCE release approached, and the most recent slot, the 14:00Z hour, published Tail 22 with Stress 69.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to hold at 23 through the European close, ease to 22 in the mid-afternoon lull, then widen to 24 for the 19:00Z-20:00Z power hour where final-day-of-Q3 market-on-close imbalances overlap the cash close. It then falls back into the low band after the close and across the Asian hours, reaching its low point in the quietest overnight stretch, before firming again through the European session of October 1 and into the 12:30Z jobless claims release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing print, which closes the window at 23. No forecast hour reaches the 25 block threshold. Non-farm payrolls on October 2 falls beyond this window.

forecast.analysis: Observed: NDX 30556.73 (+0.72%) sits about 61 points below the 30617.74 session high and has not extended in the last hour, while the 10-year yield has reversed its post-PCE dip to 5.28, the top of its 5.20-5.28 range, and SOX is -0.31% near its session low. Retracement is occurring, so a one-way path is not established.

forecast.analysis: The European cash close at 15:30Z has already passed, so index liquidity thins through this hour while the US session continues. The divergence observed at the cutoff is equities firm against a rising long end and softer semiconductors. A push above 30617.74 or a break of 30415.16 would be the first evidence either way; neither is observed yet.

Unresolved range between 30415.16 and 30617.74
Long-end yields, not the inflation print, are setting the tone
Narrow leadership: Dow near flat while NDX leads

forecast.analysis: The post-European-close lull typically reduces directional efficiency, which conditionally favours two-way rotation rather than trend continuation. If the index instead holds near the upper end of the day range on shrinking pullbacks, that would be a Tail amplifier; absent that, the mid-afternoon drift is the lower-risk part of the session.
drivers: Mid-afternoon US lull historically lowers directional efficiency
Watch whether pullbacks shrink or deepen from here
Semiconductor confirmation still absent at the hour open

forecast.analysis: Positioning for the quarter-end cash close begins to build in this hour without the imbalance itself being visible yet. Risk stays in the watch band because the observed path into the afternoon has retraced rather than extended; the conditional concern is a late one-way drift as rebalancing flow accumulates.
drivers: Pre-close quarter-end positioning builds ahead of 20:00Z
Imbalance direction is not observable this early
Conditional risk is a late drift, not observed continuation

forecast.analysis: Highest-risk hour of this window: the power hour overlaps final-day-of-Q3 rebalancing, so market-on-close imbalances concentrate here. Tail widens within the watch band because a rebalancing-driven push can deny retracement for a sustained stretch, but the direction is conditional and not yet observable.
drivers: Power hour overlaps quarter-end market-on-close imbalance
Final session of Q3 concentrates rebalancing into the close
Imbalance flow can suppress retracement for a sustained stretch
Long end at multi-decade highs raises the stakes of a late repricing

forecast.analysis: The 20:00Z cash close falls in this hour and imbalance flow unwinds into thinner post-close futures liquidity. Any structure set by the rebalancing print is conditionally prone to partial reversal once the auction clears, which usually restores two-way behaviour rather than extending a trend.
drivers: Quarter-end cash close prints at 20:00Z
Post-close futures liquidity thins sharply
Auction-driven structure often partially reverses afterwards

forecast.analysis: First full post-close hour of the new quarter's positioning. With the quarter-end mechanical flow behind, the conditional driver reverts to the bond market: a long end that stays near 5.28 keeps pressure on valuations, while a retreat would relieve it. No live structure is observed for this hour.
drivers: Quarter-end mechanical flow has cleared
Long-end direction becomes the dominant conditional driver
Thin post-close tape favours range behaviour

forecast.analysis: Late US evening typically returns to range behaviour and the mapped state eases to the low band on conditional grounds. The residual risk is a delayed repricing of today's strong ADP and Chicago PMI prints in the front end, which would show up first in yields rather than in the index.
drivers: Late-evening liquidity favours mean reversion
Delayed front-end repricing of ADP and Chicago PMI is the residual risk
No event scheduled in this hour

forecast.analysis: Quietest stretch before the Asian handover, with no scheduled catalyst. Conditionally the lowest-risk part of the window. A gap or abnormal opening structure at the Asian handover would be the first invalidation of that view, but nothing of the kind is observed at this cutoff.
drivers: No scheduled catalyst in this hour
Pre-Asian handover is conditionally the quietest stretch
Watch for abnormal structure at the handover as an invalidation

forecast.analysis: The Asian session opens the first day of Q4, which can bring fresh allocation flow rather than continuation of the Q3 close. Risk stays low on conditional grounds because index moves in this hour are usually range-bound; the checkpoint is whether Treasury futures extend the prior session's long-end move.
drivers: First Asian session of Q4 may bring new allocation flow
Treasury futures direction is the hour's checkpoint
Asian index hours are usually range-bound for NQ

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session with no US catalyst. Oil remains the live cross-asset variable given the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption, and Asian hours are when energy headlines have historically repriced first. Absent such a headline this hour is conditionally quiet.
drivers: Unresolved Hormuz disruption keeps energy headline risk live
Energy headlines have historically repriced first in Asian hours
No US catalyst scheduled

forecast.analysis: Deepest part of the overnight session. Conditional risk is at its lowest across the window because liquidity is thin but flow is usually balanced, and no scheduled release falls here. Thin liquidity can exaggerate a headline-driven move, which is the one invalidation to watch.
drivers: Lowest scheduled-catalyst density of the window
Thin liquidity can exaggerate any headline move
Flow is usually balanced in this stretch

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hours ahead of the European handover. The conditional path remains range-bound. The specific checkpoint for this hour is whether the Japanese and Korean semiconductor complex confirms or contradicts today's observed SOX weakness, since that is what has been denying NDX confirmation.
drivers: Asian semiconductor complex is this hour's confirmation checkpoint
Today's observed SOX weakness is the reference to confirm or reject
Range behaviour expected into the European handover

forecast.analysis: Pre-European hours with no scheduled US data. Conditional risk stays in the low band. If the overnight session has held near the prior day's highs on shallow pullbacks by this point, that would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of the new session; it is not observed at this cutoff.

forecast.analysis: European pre-open positioning begins and index liquidity starts to rebuild. Mode shifts to mixed because cross-asset direction is usually re-established here, with the long end the variable that matters most given the 30-year at its highest since 2002 at this cutoff.
drivers: European pre-open rebuilds index liquidity
Long-end level is the key cross-asset variable into the open

forecast.analysis: European equity open. Risk firms slightly because the open re-establishes directional flow and any overnight gap gets tested here. The conditional amplifier is a European open that extends the prior close without retracing; a gap that fills is the ordinary, lower-risk outcome.

Overnight gap, if any, is typically tested in this hour
Extension without retracement would be the amplifier to watch

forecast.analysis: First full European session hour of October. Confidence firms slightly as live price-path evidence accumulates for the new session. Conditional risk stays in the low band; European hours rarely produce the sustained no-retracement structure that Tail measures without a US catalyst.

Today's strong ADP print raises the market's sensitivity to the claims number, which is a checkpoint rather than an observed condition.

The conditional concern is that two firm labour and activity prints in succession would push the long end higher again, and it is the long end rather than the releases themselves that has been pressuring valuations at this cutoff.

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the US data block. Stress edges up with event proximity while Tail stays in the low band, because event importance and forecast dispersion are not evidence of a pathological price path. Pre-release structure is typically compressed rather than trending.

The published scores treat the release as a checkpoint; the actual path will only be scoreable after the print, and a hypothetical post-release chain is deliberately not counted as already observed.

Initial post-release repricing is usually two-way; the conditional amplifier is a release that confirms today's strong ADP and pushes the front end higher without an equity retracement.

Tail sits at the top of the watch band because an ISM beat landing on an already-firm long end is the most credible second-leg mechanism in this window.
